# Community code of conduct

Urban Heat Democratization welcomes residents, educators, researchers, planners, designers, and engineers. Participation should make evidence and decisions more understandable and open to challenge.

## Expected conduct

- Treat people and their lived experience with respect, including when questioning a claim or method.
- Critique evidence, assumptions, and code with specifics; avoid personal attacks.
- Credit contributors and sources accurately.
- Protect private information. Share only data that you have the right to publish.
- Make room for people affected by heat decisions, including those without technical credentials.

Harassment, threats, discriminatory language, doxxing, and repeated disruption are not acceptable in issues, pull requests, discussions, or project events.

## Reporting and response

For a conduct concern, [contact the maintainer privately](https://ai-aarti.com/). Do not post identifying details in a public issue. The maintainer may ask for context, remove harmful content, close or lock a thread, or limit participation. Reports will be handled with discretion, though confidentiality cannot be guaranteed when action requires involving others. If the maintainer is involved in the concern, use GitHub's [abuse reporting process](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/github-abuse-and-harassment-policy) instead.

This policy applies to project spaces and to conduct that directly affects participation in the project.
